section_1.title: Prerequisite: Average Speed vs. Instantaneous Speed
section_1.content: Define average rate of change as the slope of a secant line between two points. Use a visual of a Cheetah running to explain that speed varies over time, leading to the need for a more precise measurement at a single moment.
section_1.example: A Cheetah runs 100 meters in 5 seconds; its average speed is 20 m/s, but its speedometer fluctuated during the sprint.

section_2.title: Visualizing the Limit Process
section_2.content: Introduce the 'Zoom-in' effect. Show the secant line between two points on a curve. Gradually bring the two points closer together (Δx → 0). Visually transform the secant line into a tangent line.
section_2.example: An animation showing two points on a parabolic path (f(x)=x²) getting infinitely close until the secant line snaps into the tangent line at a specific point.

section_3.title: Defining the Derivative
section_3.content: Formally define the derivative as the limit of the difference quotient: f'(x) = lim(h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Connect this directly to the slope of the tangent line at point x.
section_3.example: Algebraic derivation for f(x) = x², showing the resulting slope formula is 2x.

section_4.title: Application: The Instantaneous Velocity
section_4.content: Apply the concept to motion. If position is s(t), the derivative s'(t) gives the instantaneous velocity. This demonstrates the practical utility of derivatives in physics.
section_4.example: A drone taking off; use the derivative of its height function to calculate its exact velocity at the 2-second mark.

section_5.title: Summary and Conclusion
section_5.content: Recap that the derivative is simply the 'slope function.' Emphasize that it captures 'instantaneous change' by taking the limit as the interval of change shrinks to zero.
section_5.example: A final infographic showing: Secant (Average) -> Tangent (Instantaneous) -> Derivative.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Shift right to give room to the left-side lecture text
                x = 2.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2

        # Persistent objects
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 5, 1], y_range=[0, 10, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        func = lambda t: 0.5 * t**2
        graph = axes.plot(func, color=BLUE)
        axes_graph_group = VGroup(axes, graph)
        
        # Using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/drone.svg]

        drone.next_to(axes_graph_group, UP)

        self.wait(1)
